correctness.rationale: Identical unit additive valuations make EF1 equivalent to balanced bundle sizes. The cost C=1/2Σ_j(s_j²−Σ_t x_tj²) is minimized by maximizing Σx² over integral transportation matrices. A support cycle permits ±1 alternating perturbations, both feasible, with sum of squared objectives strictly increasing, ruling out cycles for every optimum. Any forest gives at most r−1 mixed agent columns. Equal (r−1)-sized r parts with r−1 agents force equality. For r=2, a+b=nq and a mod q=d imply no or exactly one mixed bundle and cost d(q−d). Independent enumerations checked 144 positive small cases and 1,771 occupancy matrices; no finite proof substitution.
residual_risks: Multipartite bound all r, any agent count; numerical cost formula only r=2 and divisibility a+b=nq.
